string.name: about_p_what
string.value: Reverb is a lightweight podcast client with an ink-and-wash aesthetic. Discover shows, subscribe, download for offline, and resume anytime — focused on listening.

string.name: about_p_features
string.value:
· Discover: browse daily charts by region and category; reorder and swipe between categories
· Search: find shows or episodes by keyword, or paste an RSS URL
· Video links: paste a Bilibili video link or BV ID and listen to it as an episode (no sign-in; episodes from video links cannot be downloaded)
· Share shows: create an image with the show artwork, title, description and Reverb branding
· Radio: roam at random or follow time-of-day moods
· Live radio: keep your favourite internet radio streams, search an online directory (radio-browser.info), or add from the built-in selection; tap to listen. On the player page you can cast the sound to a TV or speaker on the same Wi-Fi (this platform uses the system cast picker)
· Updates: every episode from the shows you follow, newest first, on its own tab
· Library: six shelves — subscriptions, up next, favorites, downloads, history and notes
· Batch and shortcuts: tap an episode cover to open its channel; in Updates, Favorites, Downloads, History or a channel page, long-press a row and pick "Select multiple" to add the whole batch to Up next
· Offline: download episodes to this device, optionally Wi-Fi only
· Playback cache: episodes you play stay on this device and replay offline; loaded lists and artwork stay browsable without a connection, clearable in Settings
· Playback: speed, skip, sleep timer, play modes (sequential / repeat one / shuffle), resume, background and lock screen controls
· Transcript: on-device transcription (Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean and Cantonese), or read the publisher’s transcript when provided; full-text search and export as text or Markdown to share
· Notes: mark the second a line lands on you and write a word about it; the Notes shelf turns them into a timeline you can tap back into
· Show notes: swipe on the player page
· Chapters: for episodes whose publisher ships a chapter list, the current chapter appears above the seek bar; tap to jump. The list is cached once fetched, so it works offline
· Update reminders: get notified when a new episode lands
· System backup: subscriptions, favorites, history, download records (links only), stamps, notes, listening stats and settings are backed up by the OS and migrate with device changes; audio and transcripts are not included
· Appearance: dark/light/system, text size, accent colour, multiple languages

string.name: about_p_philosophy
string.value:
The look draws on ink wash, celadon and beam gold; the name and icon echo "lingering sound" — a wave wrapping a roof beam.

Sourcing stays free end to end, with no login and no API key: discovery uses public directories including Apple, fyyd and gpodder, while playback always comes back to the publisher's own RSS and streams the original audio.

Privacy: subscriptions, history and downloads stay on your device, are not automatically uploaded to the developer, and are not used for cross-app tracking.

string.name: privacy_consent_body
string.value:
Reverb processes most data on your device. It has no developer backend, account, ads, analytics, attribution, third-party login or push, crash reporting, or cross-app tracking. Subscriptions, history, favorites, downloads, playback cache, listening statistics, settings, a random installation ID, and runtime logs are processed locally and are not automatically uploaded to the developer. The HarmonyOS app uses system capabilities and first-party code. Since 1.0.2, if backup is enabled in system settings (HarmonyOS Backup & Restore, system cloud space, or Phone Clone), the operating system copies subscriptions, favorites, history, download records (links only), stamps, notes, listening statistics, and settings to your own system cloud account or new device; audio, transcript and chart caches, and logs are not included, and the switch lives in system settings.

When online, search terms, region, or category are sent to public directories such as Apple, fyyd, and gpodder. RSS, artwork, audio, and transcripts are requested directly from publishers or hosts, which exposes your IP address, User-Agent, and requested resource to them. Logs may contain show or episode identifiers and the host names of accessed services; they leave the app only when you choose to share or export them. Read the full policy for details.

Tapping "Agree and continue" means you have read and accept this policy.

string.name: privacy_consent_video
string.value: Video links (optional). Paste a video page link or a BV ID into the search field and that video is played as an episode: the app asks the video site’s public API (api.bilibili.com) for the title, cover and audio address, then streams from its content delivery network (*.bilivideo.com and similar) and caches the audio locally like any other episode. The requests do not sign in and carry no user identifiers; to obtain the audio address they are sent with a browser User-Agent and the video site’s referring page, so the site sees those and your IP address. Episodes from video links cannot be downloaded; their automatic cache is cleared together with everything else by “Clear cache”.

string.name: privacy_consent_auth
string.value: Private feeds (optional). Some self-hosted RSS feeds require a username and password (HTTP Basic authentication). When such a feed asks, the app prompts once and sends those credentials back only to that feed’s own host (including its subdomains), for its RSS, audio, downloads and official transcripts — never to an unrelated audio CDN. Credentials are stored only on this device, are not included in backups, OPML exports or logs, and are deleted when you unsubscribe. A plain http:// feed sends the password unencrypted; prefer https://.

string.name: privacy_consent_asr
string.value: Offline speech-to-text. This build bundles offline speech recognition (the open-source sherpa-onnx runtime with the SenseVoiceSmall model). Turning an episode’s audio into text happens entirely on your device — the audio is never uploaded, never leaves the device, and never passes through any server. Transcription currently supports Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean and Cantonese. You can turn this off in Settings.

string.name: privacy_consent_lan
string.value: Local network sync (optional). After you open “Local network sync” in Settings, the app advertises a service name (including this device's name and a short random identifier) on the same Wi-Fi and temporarily opens a TCP port; both stop when the page closes. After you tap the other device or enter its address, each device shows a six-digit pairing code, and transfer starts only when you confirm both screens match. The transfer carries the same six sections as a full backup (subscriptions, favourites, stamps, notes, history and listening stats, with stats merged per device); it excludes audio, binary caches, private-feed usernames and passwords, app settings and the play queue. Data is encrypted with keys negotiated between the two devices (ECDH P-256 and AES-256-GCM) and goes directly only between the two paired devices — never through any server, and never uploaded to the developer. Deletions also sync: when you unsubscribe, remove a favorite, or delete a stamp or note on one device, this device records which kind, which item and when, and sends it with the sync so the other device deletes it too; the record stays only on this device and is cleared after 90 days. A deletion record takes precedence over the other device's data: if the other device re-added the same item just before syncing, it is still deleted this time. The same connection also carries playback handoff while the page stays open: the playing device sends the current episode's title, cover and audio address, position, play state and speed once a second, and immediately on pause, seek or an episode change. When you tap “Continue on this device”, the playing device pauses first and replies with its exact position, and the other device seeks there and starts playing. This part is not written to disk on either device, is not part of any backup, never takes over or starts playback automatically, excludes live streams, and stops when the page closes.

string.name: privacy_consent_radio
string.value: Live radio and casting (optional). In the Radio tab you can add a station address manually, or search the public online radio directory (radio-browser.info) by keyword: your search term is sent only to that directory, with no login and no user identifier. After the directory returns results, the app sends one header-only request to each station address in the results so unreachable stations can be hidden; those servers will see your IP address and User-Agent. The station names and addresses you add stay on this device and travel only in a full backup you export. On the player, Cast uses the system cast picker: the system discovers TVs, speakers and other devices on the same Wi-Fi and carries the audio, while the app only hands over this playback. Device names and addresses are never uploaded to the developer and never written to logs.
